name: Gilberto LERENA (Gilberto Justiniano LERENA LENGUAS)
occupation: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO (commercial broker), per the 1895 census; breeder and co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book
source: 1895 Argentine national census, Seccion 21; and baptism act No. 1447 of 31 Oct 1886, San Francisco de Asis - IMAGE READ; and baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis, Catedral Basilica de Montevideo, 10 Sep 1885 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BQZD-W
note: *** Co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book; a Group 1 at Palermo renamed for him in 1914. A Lerena at the centre of Argentine thoroughbred breeding, in the right country at the right time - and PABLO ARMANDO TRAINED AND OWNED RACEHORSES. *** Born Montevideo 24 May 1855, died 8 December 1912. His father is now documented rather than asserted: his brother Luis Eugenio's marriage act of 19 December 1864 names their parents as Don Luis and Dona Justiniana Lenguas. That he and Luis Eugenio are BROTHERS still rests on published genealogy, not on an act, and is marked secondary on the charts. *** NO PROVEN LINK TO PABLO ARMANDO. *** *** HIS PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED, 13 September 2026: LUIS LERENA and JUSTINIANA LENGUAS. *** Two independent Uruguayan parish records, entered for two different children of his, both give his parents so. That makes him A BROTHER OF LUIS EUGENIO LERENA LENGUAS - the same Montevideo household that produced the one Lerena baptism in Rosario before 1879. The racing dynasty and the Rosario thread are the same family. *** THE IMAGE IS NOW OPENED, AND IT IS PRIMARY. *** Act 1447 of 31 October 1886 baptises his daughter Maria Angelica Julia, "hija legitima de Don Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia Salvanach, orientales", and names the paternal grandparents "Don LUIS y Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS" - the same couple named as Luis Eugenio's parents in his marriage act of 1864 and his death act of 1901. *** AND THE GODMOTHER IS DONA JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA - Luis Eugenio's own wife, standing at the font for her husband's brother's daughter. *** The two households are one family acting as one. Written by Martin Perez, the same priest who wrote act 1720 for Candido Jaime that year. *** AND A SECOND ACT, FROM A DIFFERENT PARISH, SAYS THE SAME, 14 September 2026: *** the baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis at the Catedral Basilica on 10 September 1885 gives "abuelos paternos: Luis y Justiniana Lenguas" and "abuelos maternos: Cristobal y Angela Alvarez" - identical to act 1447, in a different year, a different parish and a different priest's hand. Its godmother is a JOSEFA LERENA otherwise unknown to this archive. *** HIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOW ASSEMBLED, 14 September 2026: EIGHT CHILDREN by Julia Salvanach *** - Gilberto (1878), Carlos (1884), Raul Alfredo Luis (1885), Maria Angelica Julia (1886), all born at Montevideo; then Maria Carlota (1890), Luis Felipe (1892), Cesar Alberto (1896) and Horacio Alfredo (1898), at Buenos Aires. *** THE LAST MONTEVIDEO BAPTISM IS 31 OCTOBER 1886 AND THE FIRST BUENOS AIRES ONE 29 OCTOBER 1890, which brackets the family's crossing between those dates *** - firmer than the "1887 to 1889" this archive read off census birthplaces. AND JUAN CARLOS IS NOT AMONG THEM. *** AND THE 1895 CENSUS SCHEDULE, READ AS A HOUSEHOLD FOR THE FIRST TIME ON 14 September 2026, GIVES HIM A TRADE: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO - a commercial broker, aged 41, casado, R. Oriental, catolico. *** This archive has had him as a breeder, which is what he is remembered for; in his own house he told the enumerator he was a broker.

name: Don Luis Eugenio LERENA LENGUAS
source: Montevideo civil death registration No. 216, 24 December 1901 - IMAGE READ; plus Rosario baptism act 1541 (1866) and Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864); and his own baptism, La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, 7 Jan 1846 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J; and the Montevideo Direccion de Cementerios mortality return for December 1901 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3QHK-XQ11-BC6G
note: *** DOCUMENTED, 13 September 2026. *** "Natural de esta Republica", married Dona Julia Juanico at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo, on 19 December 1864 - act 258, image read - which names him "hijo legitimo de Don Luis y de Dona Justiniana Lenguas". His daughter Laura Adela's baptism of 1869 names the same two as her paternal grandparents, independently. So his parentage is PRIMARY, not the tree assertion it was that morning; and it makes him a brother of GILBERTO JUSTINIANO LERENA LENGUAS, co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book - though THAT brotherhood still rests on published genealogy rather than an act, and is marked secondary on the chart. Five children, all on primary records. Died before 11 July 1910, when his widow's death was registered. *** NO LINK TO JUAN CARLOS LERENA HAS BEEN SHOWN. *** *** HIS DEATH IS FOUND: 24 DECEMBER 1901, at seven in the morning, at the house calle Suarez No. 25 in el Paso del Molino, Montevideo. *** Act 216. "De nacionalidad oriental, nacido en Montevideo, de cincuenta y seis [anos], de estado casado, y de profesion HACENDADO" - a landowner, which is the first statement of this family's standing anywhere in the archive. He died of pulmonary tuberculosis, certified by Dr Scremini. *** IT WAS HIDING UNDER A MISSPELLING: *** FamilySearch indexes him as Luis SERENA Lenguas, so every search under LERENA missed him, including a 1,502-row sweep of Montevideo Lerena deaths run the same morning. He was found by searching for his MOTHER. The act also says his father Luis Lerena was already dead, and that his mother Justiniana Lenguas was ALIVE AT 79 and staying in the same house. *** HIS OWN BAPTISM IS NOW READ: born 9 FEBRUARY 1843, baptised 7 January 1846 at the Capilla de la Mauricia, Villa de la Union. *** "Hijo legitimo de Luis Lerena y Justiniana Lenguas, ORIENTALES. Paternos: Francisco y Maria Fernandez. Maternos: Pedro y Carmen Gonzalez." Godparents Juan Lenguas and Maria Fernandez. His death act of 1901 gave his age as 56, implying 1845; the act of his own baptism is the better evidence. *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT RECORD OF THAT DEATH, 14 September 2026: *** the Montevideo cemetery office's own return, "Relacion de los individuos que han fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901", lists him against day 24 between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez. *** So he was BURIED AT MONTEVIDEO, and the date now rests on three documents - the civil act, the cemetery roll, and his widow's sworn statement of 1908. *** Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname. *** A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE REGISTER ITSELF, recorded 14 September 2026 and NOT resolved. *** Luis Eugenio's act says he was born 9 FEBRUARY 1843; his sister Justiniana Mauricia Maxima's act, the entry immediately before his on the same page in the same hand, says she was born 30 JULY 1843. *** That is FIVE AND A HALF MONTHS between two full siblings, and both cannot be right. *** Neither is a machine reading: the transcript of each act has been read verbatim, and both say "del pasado ano cuarenta y tres". *** THE ERROR IS IN THE SOURCE, NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE. *** Every act on that page is a LATER TRANSCRIPT copied out of a legajo by order of Bishop Jacinto Vera - a clerk working from loose papers three years after the events, who had already written "ano cuarenta y tres" twice on the same page. A carried-forward year is the likeliest explanation and it is a guess. Luis Eugenio's death registration of 1901 gives an age and has been read; testing it against 1843 is the next step. *** AND THE CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED THE SAME AFTERNOON - AGAINST HIS OWN BAPTISM ACT. *** Three facts, two of them already in this archive: (1) his baptism act says he was born 9 February of "el pasado ano cuarenta y tres"; (2) his sister Justiniana Mauricia's act, THE ENTRY IMMEDIATELY ABOVE HIS IN THE SAME HAND, says she was born 30 July 1843 - five and a half months before him, which is impossible; (3) *** his civil death registration of 24 December 1901 gives his age as FIFTY-SIX, which puts his birth at about 1845. *** Two independent constraints point to 1845 and only one points to 1843 - and the one is a clerk copying loose papers three years after the fact, who wrote "ano cuarenta y tres" in the entry above this one and again in the entry below. *** A YEAR CARRIED FORWARD DOWN A COLUMN IS THE ORDINARY WAY THIS ERROR HAPPENS, and it is the only reading under which his sister's date, his own death record and his baptism can all stand. *** *** SO THIS ROW NOW CARRIES 9 FEBRUARY 1845. *** The day and month are secure and are not in question; only the year moved. The act's own words are kept above and in data/1846-la-mauricia-page.tsv, because the source says 1843 and a reader is entitled to see that this archive overruled it and why. *** THIS IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DOCUMENT *** - an age at death is the weakest date in genealogy and this archive has said so in print; it is load-bearing here only because it agrees with a constraint reached independently of it.

name: Sancho LLERENA Aguilar
birthplace: Andalusia, Spain (the census says "Andaluzia"; CORDOBA comes only from a tree)
source: URUGUAY CENSUS 1726-1858, household 59 - image read; plus six indexed Uruguayan church and civil records; and NAMED IN AN ACT: the baptism of his grandson Alberto Octavio Lerena, 7 Oct 1850, S. Agustin, pueblo de la Restauracion - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZSZQ-J; and his son's marriage petition of 3 Sep 1836 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-J331-G; and as maternal grandfather in the Cordon baptism of 13 Dec 1831, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-CS9Z-2; and as a sworn witness in the Canelones marriage-investigation files 1776-1806, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W45W; and at CANELONES in 1804 as a father (baptism of Dominga Josefa, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W9V2-Y) and as a godfather (confirmation records, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-73LL-2)
note: *** NOW PARTLY PRIMARY. *** The Uruguayan census records him at Calle San Juan, Montevideo, aged 45, birthplace "ANDALUZIA", with MARIA FERNANDEZ on the line below - image opened and read. Six further indexed records name the same wife and the same children while spelling him LLERENA, LERENA, SANCIO LLERENA, D. SANCHO LERENA and LORENA. So the alternation is in the RECORDS, not in a tree. That they are all one man is still an inference, and Cordoba specifically still rests on the tree alone. *** ORIGINALLY RECORDED AS SECONDARY. *** The founder of the Montevideo Lerenas on the tree's account: a soldier from Cordoba who married Maria Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras at Canelones, 8 January 1791. His name is spelled BOTH Lerena and Llerena across forty years of Uruguayan registers, and once - in 1828 - "Sancho de Llerena". The acts have NOT been opened here. *** HE IS NOW ON AN ACT, 13 September 2026, and no longer only on an index and a published tree. *** Act 585 of 7 October 1850 names the paternal grandparents of Alberto Octavio Lerena as "D. SANCHO y Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ" - so Sancho really is the father of Don Luis Lerena, and the descent this archive marked SECONDARY is upgraded. A DISCREPANCY RECORDED AGAINST IT: two 1846 acts for other children of the same couple give the paternal grandfather as FRANCISCO, not Sancho. Those 1846 entries are LATER TRANSCRIPTS copied out of a legajo ("asi consta del Legajo conservado en este Archivo, mandado trasladar por el Sr. Obispo"), while the 1850 act is a contemporaneous parish entry - so the copy loses to the original. Everything else in both sets agrees. *** AND A THIRD ACT NAMES HIM, 14 September 2026 - the earliest yet. *** His son's marriage of 3 March 1842 gives the groom as "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO y Dona Maria Fernandez". Two acts of 1842 and 1850 now say Sancho against two 1846 entries reading Francisco, and the 1846 pair say of themselves that they are later transcripts from a legajo. *** AND A FOURTH RECORD, THE EARLIEST OF ALL: *** his son's own marriage petition of 3 September 1836, in Luis's hand and over Luis's signature - "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona Maria Fernandez". Four records now name him, across 1836, 1842 and 1850. *** The doubt raised on 13 September by two 1846 transcripts reading "Francisco" is closed: they are copies, and they are outnumbered by originals. *** *** AND TWO MORE RECORDS, 14 September 2026, neither of them about his son Luis. *** (1) He is named maternal grandfather - "SANCHO LLERENA y MARIA FERNANDEZ" - in the Cordon baptism of 13 December 1831, *** at which the godfather was DON FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC, with his wife Dona Bernardina Fragoso. *** (2) He appears in person as a sworn witness in a marriage investigation at Canelones: "presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recivio juramento". Five records now name him. *** AND THEN THE QUESTION REOPENED, the same afternoon. *** The Catedral baptism of Justa Pastora's SECOND child, October 1833 - an ORIGINAL act, not a transcript - names her parents "Maternos: FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez". So the Sancho/Francisco alternation is not simply copies against originals, which is what this archive argued an hour earlier and has now withdrawn. *** The one thing constant in every record is the wife, MARIA FERNANDEZ. *** A double forename - Sancho Francisco - would explain it all without anybody being wrong, and is the leading reading. See data/sancho-or-francisco.tsv; his own marriage act would settle it and has never been opened. *** AND THE "AGUILAR" IN HIS NAME HERE IS UNATTESTED. *** None of the eight records now assembled gives him a matronymic; a full-text search for "Llerena y Aguilar" returns thirty hits and every one is QUITO, ECUADOR - a different family. Aguilar comes from the FamilySearch Tree and from nowhere this archive has read. Kept, because the tree may rest on an act nobody here has opened, but marked. *** The forename is contested, the matronymic unsupported, and MARIA FERNANDEZ is the only part of this man's identity every record agrees on. *** *** AND HE IS NOW ATTESTED IN 1804, twenty-seven years earlier than anything this archive held two days ago. *** At Canelones on 15 May 1804 his daughter DOMINGA JOSEFA is baptised "hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA FERNANDEZ"; in the confirmation list of the same year he stands godfather to "Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ"; and in the marriage-investigation files he gives evidence under oath. *** Father, godfather and sworn witness, in one town, in one decade - and every one of those acts calls him SANCHO. *** The machine transcript renders him SANCIO on the baptism, a sixth spelling for this family.

note: *** HER SURNAME IS ORIBE, AND THIS ARCHIVE RECORDED IT WRONG TWICE. *** She was written here as Carolina OLIVA, from the 1836 marriage petition and from FamilySearch's index of it - which says Oliva, and which is where the reading came from. The Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837, a different book in a different hand, names her "Dna CAROLINA ORIBE" standing godmother with her husband to his brother's child. The 1836 petition was then re-opened and magnified: it reads ORIBE there too, with a clear b. *** And the published genealogy this archive has always tiered as SECONDARY said all along that Don Luis married firstly a daughter of an ORIBE. It was right. *** She married Luis Lerena at Montevideo in September 1836, was ALIVE IN JULY 1837, and was dead by March 1842 when he remarried "en segundas nupcias". *** ORIBE is one of the great Uruguayan names - Manuel Oribe was President 1835-1838 and founder of the Blancos - but NOTHING READ HERE MAKES HER HIS KIN. *** Oribe is a surname, not a proof, and no record yet names her parents.

source: Named as father in the Montevideo death registration of Josefa Lerena Traibel, 3 April 1947 - ark 1:1:617P-WJY6; and as maternal grandfather in two Union baptisms of 8 Mar 1880 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS46-J; and as father of the groom in the Catedral marriage of 3 Feb 1892 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-R32C-K; and TWO baptisms of his children, San Francisco de Asis, 12 Mar 1858, naming his parents - San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo, baptisms of 12 Mar 1858 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-NRM4; and his own MONTEVIDEO CIVIL DEATH REGISTRATION of 23 Aug 1890 - index read, ark 1:1:62J2-4CNQ, image 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K796-D NOT YET OPENED; and the baptism of his son ALEJANDRO at La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, 7 Jan 1846 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J
note: *** THE HEAD OF THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH, named at last on 14 September 2026. *** Husband of AMBROSIA TRAIBEL and father of Josefa Lerena Traibel, born 1851. This archive has referred to the Lerena Traibel since its first week without ever placing Avelino. *** HE IS SANCHO'S SON - SETTLED 14 September 2026 ON A PARISH ACT. *** An Avelino Lerena stood godfather at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1833 to a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter, which is suggestive and no more. No record found here names Avelino's own parents. *** AND HE IS NAMED IN A PARISH ACT, not only in a death index: *** the baptisms of his granddaughters at Union on 8 March 1880 give "abuelos maternos AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". *** A SECOND CHILD FOUND, 14 September 2026: ALFREDO, born about 1857, married at the Catedral Basilica on 3 February 1892 *** - "hijo legitimo de Don AVELINO LORENA y Dona Ambrosia Traibel". So Avelino and Ambrosia had at least JOSEFA (1851) and ALFREDO (c.1857), and probably MERCEDES, who stood godmother in 1880. *** TWO BAPTISMS OF 12 MARCH 1858 AT SAN FRANCISCO DE ASIS name the paternal grandparents of his children as SANCHO LERENA and MARIA FERNANDEZ - twice, on one page. *** So the whole LERENA TRAIBEL line descends from Sancho, and several of its members were already floating unattached in this register: Mercedes Micaela and Clorinda in the dispensation table, and JUAN ARTURO - the man this archive conflated with another Arturo in its first week and had to retract. *** And the godparents at those two fonts were LAVALLEJA - Justiniano, Constantino and Ana. *** *** AND HE NOW HAS DATES, 14 September 2026: BORN 1815, DIED 22 AUGUST 1890 at Montevideo, registered the next day. *** The registration names his parents Sancho and Maria Fernandez - an INDEPENDENT attestation of the parentage the 1858 baptisms settled, and the first record in this archive to say when Avelino lived. *** IT ALSO EXPLAINS SOMETHING THE ARCHIVE HAD ONLY NOTED AS ODD. *** At his son Alfredo's wedding in February 1892 the witness was AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, the mother, where a father would be expected. Avelino had been dead sixteen months. Three records - the 1858 fonts, this registration, and the 1892 marriage - now lock together in one order. The registration spells him LEVENA, an eighth spelling. The image has not been opened, so the dates are SECONDARY; the parentage is PRIMARY from 1858. *** AND AN ELDEST CHILD, found 14 September 2026 - by correcting one of this archive's own rows. *** ALEJANDRO, born 29 May 1843, baptised at La Mauricia on 7 January 1846, "hijo legitimo de Avelino Serena y Ambrosia Traibel" - a boy this archive had wrongly recorded as a sixth child of his brother Luis. So Avelino and Ambrosia were married before May 1843, and their known children run ALEJANDRO (1843), JOSEFA (1851), ALFREDO JUSTINIANO and ANA ROSARIO (1858), probably MERCEDES. *** And the act shows the two brothers standing as godparents for each other's children at the same font on the same morning *** - Luis and Justiniana for Alejandro, while Luis's own two were christened in the entries just above.
